note: HCV infects no ordinary lab animal, so this class went into patients on the genotype 1b replicon for potency and rat/dog PK and toxicology for dose and safety.
label: HCV protease inhibitors

engagement.note: Simeprevir (TMC435) blocked genotype 1b replicon replication at EC50 8 nM; no patient data yet.
engagement.quote: TMC435350 inhibited HCV replication in a cellular assay (subgenomic 1b replicon) with a half-maximal effective concentration (EC(50)) of 8 nM and a selectivity index of 5,875.

engagement.magnitude_basis: plasma HCV RNA decline vs replicon RNA inhibition
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Trial NCT00938899 (TMC435350-C101) has no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.
engagement.note: Simeprevir 200 mg daily cut plasma HCV RNA a median 3.9 log10 in genotype 1 patients within 5 days, as the replicon predicted.
engagement.quote: Plasma HCV-RNA levels dropped rapidly in all patients, with a median maximal reduction of 3.9-log(10) IU/mL and a median of 6 days to maximal reduction.
engagement.reason: Viral load fell as replicon predicted
engagement.judgement: Paired by me (Lin 2009 replicon, Reesink 2010 patients); viral RNA is the target's own product, so proximal tier. Replicon also predicted the genotype 3 gap, which held in patients (Moreno 2012, doi:10.1016/j.jhep.2011.12.033: 'No antiviral activity was evident for genotype 3'); not entered as a separate same-status entry.

engagement.note: Vaniprevir monotherapy produced robust viral load declines in HCV-infected chimpanzees; no patient comparison yet.
engagement.short: Chimp viral load fell on vaniprevir
engagement.quote: coadministration of the nucleoside analogue MK-0608 with the protease inhibitor MK-7009, both of which produced robust viral load declines as monotherapy, to an HCV-infected chimpanzee can achieve a cure of infection.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PubMed abstract; Europe PMC full text unavailable). Chimpanzee log decline not stated in abstract.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at the first published chimpanzee use with a member drug (vaniprevir, epub 2010-11-29). model_filed false: no chimpanzee data found in the US review bundle (vaniprevir was not filed in the US).

engagement.note: Vaniprevir 8-day monotherapy cut HCV RNA 1.8-4.6 log10 in genotype 1 patients, as the chimpanzee viral load declines predicted.
engagement.quote: After 1 week of vaniprevir, the decrease in HCV RNA from baseline ranged from 1.8 to 4.6 log₁₀IU/ml across all treatment groups
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both sides. Trial NCT not given in the abstract, so registry_date not found.
engagement.magnitude_basis: plasma HCV RNA log10 decline, chimpanzee vs patients (chimp decline unquantified in abstract)
engagement.reason: Patient viral load fell as in chimps
engagement.judgement: Paired by me (Olsen 2011 chimpanzee, Lawitz 2013 patients). The grazoprevir pair agrees within 2x on the log scale and changes no status: chimps 4-5 log10 at 1 mg/kg bid for 7 days (Summa 2012, doi:10.1128/AAC.00324-12) vs patients 4.74 log10 at 100 mg qd GT1 (NCT00998985, results posted 2016-03-02; Clin Ther 2018, doi:10.1016/j.clinthera.2018.03.002). Chimps carried only GT1, so they could not show grazoprevir's GT3 gap (2.64 log10).

engagement.note: Viral-kinetic model fed replicon EC50, plasma trough and preclinical liver-to-plasma ratio to predict 3-day PI monotherapy viral load declines.
engagement.short: VK model from replicon EC50 and liver ratio
engagement.quote: This analysis includes data for 8 NNPolIs and 14 PIs, including VL decreases from 3-day monotherapy, total plasma trough concentrations on day 3 (C(min)), replicon data
engagement.confidence_note: Opening entry at first use; the model was built after the monotherapy results it reproduces were public.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry. The cross-compound VK-PK/PD model is in silico, distinct from the replicon and rat-PK tracks: it converts replicon potency plus animal liver uptake into a predicted human viral load decline.
engagement.model: Viral-kinetic PK/PD model driven by replicon EC50, plasma trough and preclinical liver-to-plasma ratio (cross-compound)

engagement.note: Retrodiction: replicon potency plus trough failed to predict PI viral load declines; even with liver ratios, paritaprevir fell 4.07 log10, predicted 1.9.
engagement.quote: For PIs, however, predicting VL decreases using the same model and the EC(50,PS) and day 3 C(min) was not successful; a model including LPR values and the EC(50) instead of the EC(50,PS) provided a better prediction of VL decrease.
engagement.confidence_note: Full text (PMC3370793) read: Table 2 gives ABT-450/r 50 mg QD observed -4.07 vs predicted -1.9 log10; authors note several PI outliers 'perform significantly better than the prediction'.
engagement.magnitude_basis: day-3 plasma HCV RNA log10 decline, predicted -1.9 vs observed -4.07 (paritaprevir/ritonavir 50 mg QD); 2.2 log10 = ~160-fold in viral load
engagement.reason: Model under-predicted PI viral load falls
engagement.judgement: Retrodiction (all 14 PI monotherapy studies were public before 2012), so contra not neg. The protein-shifted replicon version failed outright; the LPR-refit version still missed paritaprevir, danoprevir-class outliers by >2 log10. GS-9256, vedroprevir (GS-9451) and narlaprevir are in the dataset without a model prediction.
engagement.model: Viral-kinetic PK/PD model driven by replicon EC50, plasma trough and preclinical liver-to-plasma ratio (cross-compound)

dose.model: Replicon EC99 vs rat plasma and liver exposure
dose.note: Rat plasma and liver levels 8 h after dosing exceeded the replicon EC99, the exposure target carried into first-in-human.
dose.quote: Compound concentrations detected in both plasma and liver at 8 h postdosing were above the EC(99) value measured in the replicon.

dose.magnitude_basis: once-daily plasma exposure vs replicon EC99 target
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the abstract does not give trough-to-EC99 ratios, so whether the numeric target was met is inferred from the antiviral response.
dose.model: Replicon EC99 vs rat plasma and liver exposure
dose.note: Healthy-volunteer PK supported once-daily dosing up to 600 mg with no serious adverse events, and 200 mg daily gave potent antiviral activity in patients.
dose.quote: Once daily TMC435 given orally was generally safe and well tolerated and demonstrated potent antiviral activity.
dose.judgement: Scored same under the 'reached, drug worked' row: the regimen carried in at the rat-PK/replicon target produced the predicted response, and the drug later worked in Phase 3. Not margin_stated: the abstract states no NOAEL. Glecaprevir's review (209394 PharmR) states a 70x NOAEL margin at 300 mg, which held; not entered separately to avoid a same-status repeat. Reddy 2012 (doi:10.1128/AAC.06283-11, 14 PIs) found plasma trough/protein-shifted EC50 did not rank-order 3-day viral declines without liver-to-plasma ratios; a retrospective magnitude analysis, not scored.

efficacy.note: Replicon showed simeprevir synergistic with interferon and additive with ribavirin, the regimen later tested.
efficacy.quote: The compound was synergistic with alpha interferon and an NS5B inhibitor in the replicon model and additive with ribavirin.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: SVR12 vs replicon EC50 fold change (Q80K FC 11)
efficacy.confidence_note: Label read in full from the source bundle (sections 5.1, 12.4, 14).
efficacy.note: QUEST 1/2: SVR12 80% vs 50% on placebo; Q80K, which cut replicon potency 11-fold, cut SVR12 to 58% vs 84%.
efficacy.quote: In the OLYSIO treatment group, SVR12 rates were lower in subjects with genotype 1a virus with the NS3 Q80K polymorphism at baseline compared to subjects infected with genotype 1a virus without the Q80K polymorphism.

patient_trials.quote: An Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability Study of TMC435 in Treatment-naive, Genotype 1 Hepatitis C-infected Patients

efficacy.reason: SVR rose; Q80K loss as predicted
efficacy.judgement: comparison_stated true because the label ties the clinical Q80K loss to its microbiology section (12.4) that gives the replicon fold change. Year is the label (Nov 2013), before QUEST-1 results posted (2014-06-04). No member failed on efficacy in patients (faldaprevir stopped commercially; sovaprevir for safety), so not neg.

efficacy.note: Mice carrying a high frequency of NS3-D168 variants failed asunaprevir and daclatasvir plus asunaprevir; low-frequency mice cleared virus. No patient comparison yet.
efficacy.quote: Mice with high frequencies of NS3-D168 showed low susceptibility to asunaprevir treatment and failed to respond to daclatasvir plus asunaprevir therapy.
efficacy.population: HCV genotype 1b, prior simeprevir failure (NS3-D168 variants)
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level prediction: which patients (those carrying protease-inhibitor resistance from a prior simeprevir failure) will not respond to an asunaprevir regimen. model_first_use_year 2015 is a proxy: the first member-drug use found; the mouse was used with telaprevir earlier. The paper says the patient effect was not yet known, so the prediction is prospective.
efficacy.model: Human hepatocyte chimeric mouse (uPA/SCID) infected with patient HCV genotype 1b

efficacy.note: Patients who had failed simeprevir responded worse to daclatasvir plus asunaprevir, and their sera re-selected D168 variants in mice, as predicted.
efficacy.quote: Virological response to daclatasvir plus asunaprevir treatment was significantly lower in patients with simeprevir treatment failure as compared to those without previous treatment.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Single-centre Japanese cohort, not a registered trial, so no registry_date; response rates not given in the abstract.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: virological response to daclatasvir plus asunaprevir, prior-PI-failure vs PI-naive
efficacy.population: HCV genotype 1b, prior simeprevir failure (NS3-D168 variants)
efficacy.reason: Prior PI failure predicted poor response
efficacy.judgement: comparison_stated true: the same paper reports the patient cohort and chimeric mice infected with those patients' sera. retrodiction false because the status rests on the 2015 mouse prediction, made before this patient result; the 2016 mouse arm itself ran after the patients failed and is not scored separately. Endpoint is the cohort's virological response (SVR) to the regimen, not a pre-specified trial endpoint.
efficacy.model: Human hepatocyte chimeric mouse (uPA/SCID) infected with patient HCV genotype 1b

safety.confidence_note: Label section 13 read in full. model_first_use_year 2007 is a proxy: first-in-human trial NCT00938899 started 2007-01, so GLP toxicology preceded it.
safety.note: Simeprevir: dog heart necrosis at 28x and rat testicular findings at 0.2x human exposure; label states no patient comparison.
safety.quote: Cardiovascular toxicity consisting of acute endocardial and myocardial necrosis restricted to the left ventricular subendocardial area was seen in 2 out of 6 animals in a 2-week oral dog toxicity study

safety.magnitude_basis: AUC multiple: animal hepatobiliary toxicity at >=74x (no effect at >=3x) vs ALT >5xULN in 1% at 1x
safety.confidence_note: FDA pharmacology review (208261 PharmR) and label section 5.1 read from the source bundle.
safety.note: Grazoprevir hepatobiliary toxicity in mice and dogs (bilirubin, ALT) matched late ALT elevations in 1% of patients, rising with plasma exposure.
safety.short: Liver signal in mice, dogs, patients
safety.quote: The main target organs of toxicity identified following oral GZR administration were the liver and gallbladder (mice and dogs), with related hepatobiliary findings also observed in clinical trials.
safety.judgement: Same in kind, stated by FDA. The margin was misplaced (toxic dose >=74x in animals; ALT >5xULN in 1% of patients at clinical exposure) but the dose was not blocked, so it stays in safety rather than dose (decision 16). Hepatic decompensation in Child-Pugh B/C cirrhosis (class-wide FDA warnings) is not scored: healthy animals cannot show it.
